accepted_phrases: Keep the failure branches separate. The unnamed clear-case owner reports clarity after two years, not a material diagnosis or protection result. One Apple Leather Cases participant reports corner degradation at about two years, while one OtterBox Symmetry owner reports a thin silicone strip breaking after about three years of pulling the phone from a pocket. General leather evidence says temperature and humidity variation can contribute to cracks, handling affects deterioration, and finishes can become tacky; it does not establish the cause or timing of those phone-case corners. General plastic evidence lists polyurethane as capable of yellowing, brittleness, stickiness, crumbling, and hydrolysis weakening; it can explain why a soft-touch surface might become gummy but cannot identify the exact coating or predict its lifetime. Therefore yellowing, corner wear, tackiness, fit, and geometry failure need their own evidence and cannot be transferred across materials or products.

Preserve every owner report at its actual scope. The clear case is unnamed and reports two-year clarity only. The Apple Leather Cases report reaches about two years and records corner degradation. The OtterBox Symmetry report reaches about three years and records breakage at a heavily used thin strip. The Casetify report covers more than one year, multiple uncontrolled drops, an undinged case, and bright unscratched graphics but no exact model. One Spigen comment describes about four years as a Pixel user rather than continuous use of one identified case, and another says only that an unspecified Spigen was used for years on a Samsung. The OtterBox warranty and component-failure report has no precise model or duration. These anecdotes can identify possible outcomes and inspection points, but they are not standardized tests, population rates, or one combined four-year observation.

Treat the CASEKOO page as a current seller-claim snapshot. It lists a 25.99 dollar iPhone 13 Pro Max clear case with a rigid polycarbonate back, TPU bumpers, an anti-yellow coating said to resist 99.9 percent of yellowing caused by ultraviolet light and sweat, military-level drop-protection language, and free replacement within one year. Polycarbonate can yellow under ultraviolet exposure and may use stabilizers or coatings, while TPU formulations differ and aliphatic TPU is used when stable light color is required. Those material sources make formulation and coating details relevant, but neither they nor the product page independently verify the named resin, coating performance, drop result, or four-year lifetime. The one-year replacement promise also ends well before year four.

If a purchase must be made, the listed CASEKOO case is only a conditional monitored trial, not a proven four-year recommendation. Verify the exact phone fit, model and revision, written warranty, resin or coating documentation, and any underlying test method rather than inferring them from generic PC or TPU labels. Before use, photograph the case against the same neutral background and lighting and record corner, port, lip, and retention fit. Repeat photographs and fit and surface checks at a fixed interval such as every three months. Log meaningful drops with height, surface, impact area, visible case damage, and phone outcome. Inspect color shift, persistent tackiness, coating wear, cracks, looseness, corner or bumper separation, port-strip tearing, and reduced lip or retention coverage. Replace the case when cracking, looseness, separation, persistent tackiness, or reduced retention compromises fit, even if it still looks acceptable. The record can create future evidence but cannot retroactively prove four-year performance.

A year-four claim requires one exact case model observed for about four years with both acceptable appearance and protection outcomes under described use. The strongest named appearance-plus-drop report lasts only more than one year and lacks an exact model. The leather and Symmetry reports reach about two and about three years but record failures. The unnamed clear case reaches two years for clarity only. The Spigen comments do not provide an exact model with a precise continuous four-year observation. Seller anti-yellow and drop-protection language and general polymer mechanisms are not substitutes for that missing product-level history. Therefore the available material cannot identify a case proven to look acceptable and protect in year four.

No specific case in the available material is proven to remain presentable and protective in year four. Distinguish the CASEKOO seller statements from material mechanisms and both from owner observations; state the actual more-than-one-year, about-two-year, about-three-year, and imprecise durations without merging them; and keep appearance, tackiness, corner integrity, fit, and uncontrolled drop outcomes separate. If a purchase is unavoidable, the CASEKOO listing may be treated only as a conditional monitored trial because it exposes PC-and-TPU construction, anti-yellow and drop claims, and a one-year replacement promise. Verify the exact model and documentation, establish a photo and fit baseline, repeat checks on schedule, log drops, and replace on cracking, looseness, separation, persistent tackiness, or reduced retention. Do not call it or any brand a four-year winner.
No exact case model is proven to remain both presentable and protective in year four; the listed CASEKOO case is at most a conditional monitored trial, not a four-year recommendation.
Decline to name a proven four-year winner and use the listed clear case only conditionally with exact-model verification, scheduled inspection, drop logging, and replacement triggers.

The material contains a current seller page, general material mechanisms, a more-than-one-year Casetify report, about-two-year clear and leather observations, an about-three-year Symmetry failure, and imprecise or continuity-ambiguous Spigen reports, but no exact model observed for four years with both appearance and protection outcomes.

Polycarbonate, TPU, polyurethane, and leather mechanisms explain possible aging pathways and the importance of formulation, coating, environment, handling, and geometry, but they do not prove one named case's lifetime.

Reports from different owners, brands, models, durations, and use conditions cannot be pooled into a four-year result, and clarity, corner integrity, surface condition, case survival, and phone survival remain separate outcomes.

A conditional trial is acceptable only with an exact-model baseline, scheduled photographs and fit checks, drop records, and replacement when cracks, looseness, separation, persistent tackiness, or reduced retention appears.
The seller's never-yellow language proves that the CASEKOO case will remain clear for four years.
Military-level drop-protection language proves that the case will still protect properly in year four.
Any case labeled PC and TPU has the same formulation, coating, yellowing resistance, and four-year lifetime.
All polycarbonate phone cases yellow after the same fixed amount of time regardless of stabilizers, coatings, exposure, or construction.
The general polyurethane conservation page proves that the discarded soft-touch phone case had a particular formulation and failed by hydrolysis.
The general leather conservation page proves the exact cause and timing of the Apple Leather Cases corner degradation.
An unnamed clear case remaining clear for two years proves that clear cases or the listed CASEKOO case remain clear for four years.
Being a Pixel user for about four years proves that one exact Spigen case was continuously used and remained protective for four years.
No cracked phone after unspecified owner drops is equivalent to a controlled drop-protection test and population failure rate.
The one-year, two-year, three-year, and imprecise reports can be combined into one four-year test of a single phone case.
Buy the CASEKOO case as the proven four-year winner because its seller page says never yellow and military-level drop protection.
Keep using a case after cracks, looseness, bumper separation, or reduced retention as long as its color still looks acceptable.

research_subgoals.description: Audit the current clear-case listing against polycarbonate and TPU mechanisms without converting seller or material statements into a product lifetime.
Explain clear yellowing, leather corner wear, soft-touch stickiness, and thin-strip breakage as separate branches while preserving the limits of general mechanisms.
Compare every owner observation by brand or family, actual duration, exact-model specificity, failure or appearance outcome, and uncontrolled protection result.
Determine whether one exact case is observed for four years with both acceptable appearance and protection, allowing the result to remain unresolved.
Give only a conditional purchase path with exact-model verification, a reproducible baseline, scheduled inspection, drop logging, and safety-relevant replacement triggers.

query_requirements.text: Explain how polycarbonate, TPU formulation, polyurethane degradation, leather environment and handling, coatings, and geometry can lead to different visible and structural outcomes without treating a material label as a lifetime guarantee.

Audit each owner report in a compact table by brand or family, actual observation period, exact-model specificity, appearance or component failure, and observed phone protection, keeping uncontrolled anecdotes separate.

Compare the current seller claims with the owner evidence and state explicitly whether any one exact case is supported as both presentable and protective in year four; do not force a winner when that evidence is absent.

If buying now, give only a conditional choice and specify exact-model checks, baseline photographs, inspection interval, drop-log fields, failure checks, and replacement triggers that protect fit and retention rather than appearance alone.
